transcript:
[Doctor]: Hello Mr. Doe, how are you doing today?

[Patient]: Hello doctor. I’m alright, although my knee pain is really troubling me.

[Doctor]: I see. I understand you’ve been having moderate to severe pain in your left knee for the past 3 weeks. Can you tell me more about it?

[Patient]: Yes, the pain started about three weeks ago. It’s gotten pretty bad. There’s also some swelling and occasionally I hear a clicking sound.

[Doctor]: Hmm, I see. Is the pain constant or does it come and go?

[Patient]: It’s there pretty much every day. It’s really affecting my ability to stand for long periods or even walk.

[Doctor]: That sounds very uncomfortable. Have you noticed any other joint pain?

[Patient]: No, it’s just the left knee. No issues with the other joints.

[Doctor]: How about any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath?

[Patient]: No, nothing like that.

[Doctor]: Any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs?

[Patient]: No, none of that either.

[Doctor]: Alright. Overall, apart from your knee, how has your general health been?

[Patient]: I’d say I’m in good health otherwise.

[Doctor]: That’s good to hear. Can you tell me a bit about your past medical history?

[Patient]: Sure. I have osteoarthritis, and I’ve been managing it for a while. I also have hypertension.

[Doctor]: I see. Are you currently taking any medications?

[Patient]: Yes, I take Lisinopril 10 mg daily for my blood pressure. I also take over-the-counter NSAIDs when the pain gets really bad.

[Doctor]: Do you have any allergies to medications?

[Patient]: No, I don’t have any drug allergies.

[Doctor]: Alright. Can you tell me a bit about your social habits? Do you smoke or consume alcohol?

[Patient]: I’m a non-smoker. I have an occasional drink, maybe 1-2 drinks per week.

[Doctor]: How’s your diet?

[Patient]: I try to keep it balanced, but I do have fast food occasionally.

[Doctor]: How about your sleep? Are you sleeping well?

[Patient]: I usually get about 6-7 hours of sleep a night.

[Doctor]: Understood. Let’s go ahead and check your vital signs. Your blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 72 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6 °F. Everything looks stable there.

[Patient]: That’s good to know.

[Doctor]: Now, let’s take a closer look at your knee. I see some swelling and slight redness in your left knee. Does it hurt when I press here?

[Patient]: Yes, it’s quite tender there.

[Doctor]: I notice that the tenderness is over the medial joint line. How’s your range of motion? Can you bend and extend your knee for me?

[Patient]: It’s limited because of the pain, especially when I try to flex and extend it fully.

[Doctor]: I see. You also have an antalgic gait, which means you’re limping to avoid putting weight on the painful knee. I’m going to order an MRI of your left knee to evaluate for a potential meniscal tear or ligament damage. Does that sound alright?

[Patient]: Yes, that sounds good. I just want to know what’s going on.

[Doctor]: Great. In the meantime, I’m going to prescribe you some NSAIDs. Take Ibuprofen 400 mg, orally, three times daily for the next 10 days. That should help with the pain and inflammation.

[Patient]: Okay, I’ll do that.

[Doctor]: I also want you to rest your knee as much as possible. Avoid any activities that make the pain worse. Apply ice to your knee for about 20 minutes a few times a day to help reduce the swelling. Elevate your knee when you can.

[Patient]: Alright, I’ll make sure to do that.

[Doctor]: We’ll schedule a follow-up consultation in 2 weeks to reassess your condition and review the MRI results.

[Patient]: Sounds good.

[Doctor]: Do you have any questions or concerns about the treatment plan?

[Patient]: No, I think you’ve covered everything. I just hope this helps.

[Doctor]: I’m confident it will. If you experience any adverse effects from the medication or if your symptoms don’t improve, please let us know immediately.

[Patient]: I will. Thank you, doctor.

[Doctor]: You’re welcome, Mr. Doe. Take care and I’ll see you in two weeks.

[Patient]: Thank you. Have a good day.

[Doctor]: You too.
